### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
🚨 **BLOCKING: unguarded `dispatchCiWorkflow` in the zombie re-dispatch path — a throwing dispatch aborts the entire SM tick**

The zombie re-dispatch sequence strips the arm, then calls the dispatch **outside any try/catch** (js/smAgent.js:2777):

```js
try {
    if (!DRY) {
        github_remove_label({ ... label: 'ai_validating' ... });
    }
} catch (eZun) { /* absent arm is fine */ }
dropOpenPrsCache(effectiveRepoInfo);
dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);   // ← unguarded
```

Every other localAction contains its per-ticket failures: `validate_pr` wraps the **identical** `dispatchCiWorkflow` call (js/smAgent.js:2062) in its whole-body try/catch, and `headWorkflowRunsSafe` exists specifically because `cli_execute_command` throws ("a probe error must not kill the action"). If `gh workflow run` throws here — transient gh/API failure, network hiccup, auth blip — the exception propagates out of the tickets loop and `processRule` (the `rules.forEach` at js/smAgent.js:5090 has no try/catch either), **killing the whole SM tick**: every remaining rule and every remaining PR in the window is skipped for that cadence. That is exactly the merge-window-starvation class of incident gh-821 exists to eliminate, reintroduced on the degraded-infrastructure path where throws are most likely.

It also leaves the PR half-transitioned: the arm is already stripped, the dispatch failed, the re-arm never runs, and — worst — the **marker comment is never posted**, so the crash-loop counter under-counts and the 1/head/hour bound cannot fire for that lost dispatch.

Fix (mirrors the file's own convention):

```js
try {
    dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);
} catch (eZci) {
    console.warn('  ⚠️  zombie re-dispatch failed for ' + key + ': ' + (eZci.message || eZci) +
                 ' — re-arming, retry next tick');
    try {
        if (!DRY) {
            github_add_labels({
                workspace: effectiveRepoInfo.owner, repository: effectiveRepoInfo.repo,
                number: ticket.prNumber, labels: ['ai_validating']
            });
        }
    } catch (eZre2) { /* validate-armed re-arms next tick anyway */ }
    continue;
}
```

(Restore the arm on dispatch failure so the PR keeps its serialization slot and the next tick retries as a zombie instead of re-entering the arm race through `validate-armed`.)

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `classify()` JSDoc contradicts the deliberate fail-closed degeneracy**

The docstring says:

> Unknown/degraded shapes fail SAFE toward 'running' (arm stays — a missed recovery retries next tick; a wrongful re-dispatch burns CI).

But the module's own header (lines 30–36) and the `classify({})` test ("a truthy probe with NO facets reads as zombie-no-run — deliberate gh-821 bias") codify the opposite for the *realistic* degraded shape: a full probe failure yields `{ active: false, newest: null }` → **`zombie-no-run` → re-dispatch**, not `'running'`. Only a *missing* probe argument (`classify(null)`) and per-facet oddities fall safe to `'running'`.

This matters beyond wording: the next maintainer reading the `classify()` contract could "fix" the discrepancy by making degraded probes read `'running'` — which the header explicitly warns would re-create the deadlock (`the alternative (treating a probe outage as live) re-creates the deadlock this module exists to break`). Please reword the last docstring paragraph to match the implemented, tested contract, e.g.:

```

 * stays). A fully-failed probe (every facet at its catch default) reads
 * 'zombie-no-run' — the deliberate gh-821 bias documented in the header:

```

### Thread 3 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

`js/common/validationLiveness.js:46` exports `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES`, justified as "the same vocabulary hasActiveDispatchedRun / hasActiveHeadRun match in smAgent" — but nothing consumes it: `hasActiveDispatchedRun`, the `PROBE_WORKER_SOURCE` copy, and `hasActiveHeadRun` all keep their own inline `queued/in_progress/waiting/pending` lists, and no test references the constant.

# gh-821: [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)

## Description

## Goal

A validating PR whose head has no live validation run must re-dispatch within the tick instead of holding the serial `ai_validating` mutex — a cancelled/failed-concluded dispatch must never block the whole merge window.

## Subject

Tick's validating-state handling (fa `machine-sm.yml` engine + dmtools-agents arming rules). Live incident 2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z: fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`; its dispatched run concluded **cancelled** (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 guard family); the sweep kept the arm ("no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays") while four validated PRs deferred on `🔒 mutex ai_validating held`. Merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>` unstick. Instance logged on #682.

## Capability surface

- Liveness probe: for each `ai_validating` PR, resolve its head's dispatch runs; states: running (in-flight), concluded-success/failure (verdict path), cancelled/stale-with-no-run (zombie).
- Zombie rule: cancelled-only or no-run ⇒ re-dispatch validation same tick (bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`).
- Mutex fairness: the `ai_validating` mutex must be held only while a LIVE run exists; zombie ⇒ release the slot for the window (the re-dispatch re-acquires).
- Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ park `validation_failed` + comment (avoid infinite cancel-loop churn; gh-748 interplay documented).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/tick with a validating PR whose only run is cancelled ⇒ same tick re-dispatches and logs the zombie line; mutex not blocking other candidates during the same tick.
2. AC2: after 3 consecutive zombie cycles on one head ⇒ `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, no silent loop).
3. AC3: a live running validation still holds the mutex exactly as today (no behavior change for healthy flow).
4. AC4: live verification on the next cancelled-run occurrence in fa — recovery ≤ 1 tick, zero manual dispatches.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the liveness state machine (running/concluded/zombie/park).
- L2: replay the #1443 timeline (armed → cancelled → 2h hold) against the new rule — recovery at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next real occurrence recovers without manual action (I verify).

## Non-goals

- Parallel validations (serial mutex stays).
- Changing kicker/dispatch race guard gh-748 itself (zombie rule composes with it).

## References

- Instance: dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09 (fa PR #1443, runs 12:28 failure / 13:36 cancelled).
- Related: #806 (arming latch — same single-flight philosophy), #682/#748 (cancel-loop family).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 822
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/822
- **Title**: gh-821 [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-821` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +709
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:00:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T16:27:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #821
### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).
- `sm_github.json`: sweep rule description documents the amendment + knobs (`zombieRedispatchCap` default 3, `zombieRedispatchMinMs` default 3600000).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` — L1 liveness state machine (running / green / red / zombie-cancelled / zombie-no-run / fail-safe probes) + marker round-trip, per-head counts, cap/window knobs: 16 cases.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 8 sweep cases: AC1 #1443 replay (cancelled 2h ⇒ recovery at tick 1, arm re-acquired, zombie line logged), no-run zombie, AC2 crash-loop park (no 4th dispatch), bound hold + bound expiry, AC3 live-run no-churn, fresh-cancel race window preserved, DRY no-side-effects. Verified RED on the pre-fix engine (3 new behaviors fail at baseline `58a2dbf`), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2204 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes

- Probe-error degeneracy is deliberate: `newestDispatchedRun` fails closed (null), so a degraded read classifies `zombie-no-run` — worst case one bounded duplicate CI run (1/head/hour), never a wedge; a wrongful `running` classification would re-create the deadlock.
- The zombie branch composes with gh-748 (belt check: any run on the head active or completed within the dispatch-race grace keeps the arm) and leaves gh-755 / rerun-cancelled-checks untouched — fresh cancellations still read `running` for their first 15 minutes.
- AC4 (live fa verification on the next cancelled run) is owner-verified; expected recovery ≤ 2 ticks (~15-min visibility grace + one 10-min cadence) instead of a manual unstick.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | …

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #822._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
🚨 **BLOCKING: unguarded `dispatchCiWorkflow` in the zombie re-dispatch path — a throwing dispatch aborts the entire SM tick**

The zombie re-dispatch sequence strips the arm, then calls the dispatch **outside any try/catch** (js/smAgent.js:2777):

```js
try {
    if (!DRY) {
        github_remove_label({ ... label: 'ai_validating' ... });
    }
} catch (eZun) { /* absent arm is fine */ }
dropOpenPrsCache(effectiveRepoInfo);
dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);   // ← unguarded
```

Every other localAction contains its per-ticket failures: `validate_pr` wraps the **identical** `dispatchCiWorkflow` call (js/smAgent.js:2062) in its whole-body try/catch, and `headWorkflowRunsSafe` exists specifically because `cli_execute_command` throws ("a probe error must not kill the action"). If `gh workflow run` throws here — transient gh/API failure, network hiccup, auth blip — the exception propagates out of the tickets loop and `processRule` (the `rules.forEach` at js/smAgent.js:5090 has no try/catch either), **killing the whole SM tick**: every remaining rule and every remaining PR in the window is skipped for that cadence. That is exactly the merge-window-starvation class of incident gh-821 exists to eliminate, reintroduced on the degraded-infrastructure path where throws are most likely.

It also leaves the PR half-transitioned: the arm is already stripped, the dispatch failed, the re-arm never runs, and — worst — the **marker comment is never posted**, so the crash-loop counter under-counts and the 1/head/hour bound cannot fire for that lost dispatch.

Fix (mirrors the file's own convention):

```js
try {
    dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);
} catch (eZci) {
    console.warn('  ⚠️  zombie re-dispatch failed for ' + key + ': ' + (eZci.message || eZci) +
                 ' — re-arming, retry next tick');
    try {
        if (!DRY) {
            github_add_labels({
                workspace: effectiveRepoInfo.owner, repository: effectiveRepoInfo.repo,
                number: ticket.prNumber, labels: ['ai_validating']
            });
        }
    } catch (eZre2) { /* validate-armed re-arms next tick anyway */ }
    continue;
}
```

(Restore the arm on dispatch failure so the PR keeps its serialization slot and the next tick retries as a zombie instead of re-entering the arm race through `validate-armed`.)

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `classify()` JSDoc contradicts the deliberate fail-closed degeneracy**

The docstring says:

> Unknown/degraded shapes fail SAFE toward 'running' (arm stays — a missed recovery retries next tick; a wrongful re-dispatch burns CI).

But the module's own header (lines 30–36) and the `classify({})` test ("a truthy probe with NO facets reads as zombie-no-run — deliberate gh-821 bias") codify the opposite for the *realistic* degraded shape: a full probe failure yields `{ active: false, newest: null }` → **`zombie-no-run` → re-dispatch**, not `'running'`. Only a *missing* probe argument (`classify(null)`) and per-facet oddities fall safe to `'running'`.

This matters beyond wording: the next maintainer reading the `classify()` contract could "fix" the discrepancy by making degraded probes read `'running'` — which the header explicitly warns would re-create the deadlock (`the alternative (treating a probe outage as live) re-creates the deadlock this module exists to break`). Please reword the last docstring paragraph to match the implemented, tested contract, e.g.:

```
 * Missing probe / odd per-facet shapes fail SAFE toward 'running' (arm
 * stays). A fully-failed probe (every facet at its catch default) reads
 * 'zombie-no-run' — the deliberate gh-821 bias documented in the header:
 * worst case one bounded duplicate CI run, never a wedge.
```

---

### Thread 3 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` is a dead export**

`js/common/validationLiveness.js:46` exports `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES`, justified as "the same vocabulary hasActiveDispatchedRun / hasActiveHeadRun match in smAgent" — but nothing consumes it: `hasActiveDispatchedRun`, the `PROBE_WORKER_SOURCE` copy, and `hasActiveHeadRun` all keep their own inline `queued/in_progress/waiting/pending` lists, and no test references the constant.

Either wire it as the single source of truth (pass it into the helpers, or at least use it inside `classify`'s defensive branch), or drop it — an unused exported "vocabulary parity" constant invites drift exactly where parity is the point.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: two new zombie guard branches have no test coverage**

The suite covers AC1/AC2/AC3, the bound hold/expiry, no-run, and DRY — but two new behavior branches in the recovery path are untested:

1. **The gh-748 belt** (js/smAgent.js:2683–2689): a zombie-classified head with a run active/completed within `dispatchRaceGraceMs` must keep the arm and dispatch nothing (`'zombie read raced a fresh CI order'`). Test shape: `oldRun('cancelled', HEAD)` older than 15 min **plus** a fresh run on the head via the `actions/runs?head_sha=` (non-event-filtered) probe response.

2. **The `!ticket.branch` bail-out** (js/smAgent.js:2758–2762): an armed PR with no head branch must keep the arm and dispatch nothing. Cheap to add: `prItem(n, { labels: ['ai_validating'], headSha: HEAD })` with no `branch` (as the AC3 test already does).

# gh-821: [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)

## Description

## Goal

A validating PR whose head has no live validation run must re-dispatch within the tick instead of holding the serial `ai_validating` mutex — a cancelled/failed-concluded dispatch must never block the whole merge window.

## Subject

Tick's validating-state handling (fa `machine-sm.yml` engine + dmtools-agents arming rules). Live incident 2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z: fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`; its dispatched run concluded **cancelled** (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 guard family); the sweep kept the arm ("no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays") while four validated PRs deferred on `🔒 mutex ai_validating held`. Merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>` unstick. Instance logged on #682.

## Capability surface

- Liveness probe: for each `ai_validating` PR, resolve its head's dispatch runs; states: running (in-flight), concluded-success/failure (verdict path), cancelled/stale-with-no-run (zombie).
- Zombie rule: cancelled-only or no-run ⇒ re-dispatch validation same tick (bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`).
- Mutex fairness: the `ai_validating` mutex must be held only while a LIVE run exists; zombie ⇒ release the slot for the window (the re-dispatch re-acquires).
- Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ park `validation_failed` + comment (avoid infinite cancel-loop churn; gh-748 interplay documented).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/tick with a validating PR whose only run is cancelled ⇒ same tick re-dispatches and logs the zombie line; mutex not blocking other candidates during the same tick.
2. AC2: after 3 consecutive zombie cycles on one head ⇒ `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, no silent loop).
3. AC3: a live running validation still holds the mutex exactly as today (no behavior change for healthy flow).
4. AC4: live verification on the next cancelled-run occurrence in fa — recovery ≤ 1 tick, zero manual dispatches.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the liveness state machine (running/concluded/zombie/park).
- L2: replay the #1443 timeline (armed → cancelled → 2h hold) against the new rule — recovery at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next real occurrence recovers without manual action (I verify).

## Non-goals

- Parallel validations (serial mutex stays).
- Changing kicker/dispatch race guard gh-748 itself (zombie rule composes with it).

## References

- Instance: dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09 (fa PR #1443, runs 12:28 failure / 13:36 cancelled).
- Related: #806 (arming latch — same single-flight philosophy), #682/#748 (cancel-loop family).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 822
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/822
- **Title**: gh-821 [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-821` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +709
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:00:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T16:27:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #821
### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).
- `sm_github.json`: sweep rule description documents the amendment + knobs (`zombieRedispatchCap` default 3, `zombieRedispatchMinMs` default 3600000).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` — L1 liveness state machine (running / green / red / zombie-cancelled / zombie-no-run / fail-safe probes) + marker round-trip, per-head counts, cap/window knobs: 16 cases.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 8 sweep cases: AC1 #1443 replay (cancelled 2h ⇒ recovery at tick 1, arm re-acquired, zombie line logged), no-run zombie, AC2 crash-loop park (no 4th dispatch), bound hold + bound expiry, AC3 live-run no-churn, fresh-cancel race window preserved, DRY no-side-effects. Verified RED on the pre-fix engine (3 new behaviors fail at baseline `58a2dbf`), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2204 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | …

Rules for live e2e runs:

  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything

- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #822._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
🚨 **BLOCKING: unguarded `dispatchCiWorkflow` in the zombie re-dispatch path — a throwing dispatch aborts the entire SM tick**

The zombie re-dispatch sequence strips the arm, then calls the dispatch **outside any try/catch** (js/smAgent.js:2777):

```js
try {
    if (!DRY) {
        github_remove_label({ ... label: 'ai_validating' ... });
    }
} catch (eZun) { /* absent arm is fine */ }
dropOpenPrsCache(effectiveRepoInfo);
dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);   // ← unguarded
```

Every other localAction contains its per-ticket failures: `validate_pr` wraps the **identical** `dispatchCiWorkflow` call (js/smAgent.js:2062) in its whole-body try/catch, and `headWorkflowRunsSafe` exists specifically because `cli_execute_command` throws ("a probe error must not kill the action"). If `gh workflow run` throws here — transient gh/API failure, network hiccup, auth blip — the exception propagates out of the tickets loop and `processRule` (the `rules.forEach` at js/smAgent.js:5090 has no try/catch either), **killing the whole SM tick**: every remaining rule and every remaining PR in the window is skipped for that cadence. That is exactly the merge-window-starvation class of incident gh-821 exists to eliminate, reintroduced on the degraded-infrastructure path where throws are most likely.

It also leaves the PR half-transitioned: the arm is already stripped, the dispatch failed, the re-arm never runs, and — worst — the **marker comment is never posted**, so the crash-loop counter under-counts and the 1/head/hour bound cannot fire for that lost dispatch.

Fix (mirrors the file's own convention):

```js
try {
    dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);
} catch (eZci) {
    console.warn('  ⚠️  zombie re-dispatch failed for ' + key + ': ' + (eZci.message || eZci) +
                 ' — re-arming, retry next tick');
    try {
        if (!DRY) {
            github_add_labels({
                workspace: effectiveRepoInfo.owner, repository: effectiveRepoInfo.repo,
                number: ticket.prNumber, labels: ['ai_validating']
            });
        }
    } catch (eZre2) { /* validate-armed re-arms next tick anyway */ }
    continue;
}
```

(Restore the arm on dispatch failure so the PR keeps its serialization slot and the next tick retries as a zombie instead of re-entering the arm race through `validate-armed`.)

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `classify()` JSDoc contradicts the deliberate fail-closed degeneracy**

The docstring says:

> Unknown/degraded shapes fail SAFE toward 'running' (arm stays — a missed recovery retries next tick; a wrongful re-dispatch burns CI).

But the module's own header (lines 30–36) and the `classify({})` test ("a truthy probe with NO facets reads as zombie-no-run — deliberate gh-821 bias") codify the opposite for the *realistic* degraded shape: a full probe failure yields `{ active: false, newest: null }` → **`zombie-no-run` → re-dispatch**, not `'running'`. Only a *missing* probe argument (`classify(null)`) and per-facet oddities fall safe to `'running'`.

This matters beyond wording: the next maintainer reading the `classify()` contract could "fix" the discrepancy by making degraded probes read `'running'` — which the header explicitly warns would re-create the deadlock (`the alternative (treating a probe outage as live) re-creates the deadlock this module exists to break`). Please reword the last docstring paragraph to match the implemented, tested contract, e.g.:

```
 * Missing probe / odd per-facet shapes fail SAFE toward 'running' (arm
 * stays). A fully-failed probe (every facet at its catch default) reads
 * 'zombie-no-run' — the deliberate gh-821 bias documented in the header:
 * worst case one bounded duplicate CI run, never a wedge.
```

---

### Thread 3 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` is a dead export**

`js/common/validationLiveness.js:46` exports `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES`, justified as "the same vocabulary hasActiveDispatchedRun / hasActiveHeadRun match in smAgent" — but nothing consumes it: `hasActiveDispatchedRun`, the `PROBE_WORKER_SOURCE` copy, and `hasActiveHeadRun` all keep their own inline `queued/in_progress/waiting/pending` lists, and no test references the constant.

Either wire it as the single source of truth (pass it into the helpers, or at least use it inside `classify`'s defensive branch), or drop it — an unused exported "vocabulary parity" constant invites drift exactly where parity is the point.

---

### Thread 4 — `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: two new zombie guard branches have no test coverage**

The suite covers AC1/AC2/AC3, the bound hold/expiry, no-run, and DRY — but two new behavior branches in the recovery path are untested:

1. **The gh-748 belt** (js/smAgent.js:2683–2689): a zombie-classified head with a run active/completed within `dispatchRaceGraceMs` must keep the arm and dispatch nothing (`'zombie read raced a fresh CI order'`). This is the promised "composes with gh-748" guarantee from the PR description — a regression here re-creates duplicate dispatches in the kicker race window. Test shape: `oldRun('cancelled', HEAD)` older than 15 min **plus** a fresh run on the head via the `actions/runs?head_sha=` (non-event-filtered) probe response.

2. **The `!ticket.branch` bail-out** (js/smAgent.js:2758–2762): an armed PR with no head branch must keep the arm and dispatch nothing. Cheap to add: `prItem(n, { labels: ['ai_validating'], headSha: HEAD })` with no `branch` (as the AC3 test already does).

Both are pure-mock tests in the existing style (assert `!dispatched(...)`, arm stays, no comments).

### Thread 5 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: zombie park comment could surface an older green run on the head (`sProbe.green`)**

The crash-loop park (js/smAgent.js:2725) is fail-closed by design, and the newest-run-cancelled classification is the progression-safe choice. But when the head carries an **older concluded-green** dispatched run (`sProbe.green === true` — the exact facet the gh-751 strip and validate-armed's latch-skip treat as a consumable verdict), a repeated-cancel storm can park a possibly-merge-eligible head with a comment that only says "a new push restarts validation".

Consider appending a line to the park comment when `sProbe && sProbe.green`:

```js
' An older GREEN dispatched run exists on this head (gh-751/latch-skip ' +
'semantics) — worth a manual look before re-dispatching or pushing.'
```

One line, no behavior change — it just tells the human resolving the park that the head may already be merge-eligible.

# gh-821: [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)

## Description

## Goal

A validating PR whose head has no live validation run must re-dispatch within the tick instead of holding the serial `ai_validating` mutex — a cancelled/failed-concluded dispatch must never block the whole merge window.

## Subject

Tick's validating-state handling (fa `machine-sm.yml` engine + dmtools-agents arming rules). Live incident 2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z: fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`; its dispatched run concluded **cancelled** (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 guard family); the sweep kept the arm ("no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays") while four validated PRs deferred on `🔒 mutex ai_validating held`. Merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>` unstick. Instance logged on #682.

## Capability surface

- Liveness probe: for each `ai_validating` PR, resolve its head's dispatch runs; states: running (in-flight), concluded-success/failure (verdict path), cancelled/stale-with-no-run (zombie).
- Zombie rule: cancelled-only or no-run ⇒ re-dispatch validation same tick (bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`).
- Mutex fairness: the `ai_validating` mutex must be held only while a LIVE run exists; zombie ⇒ release the slot for the window (the re-dispatch re-acquires).
- Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ park `validation_failed` + comment (avoid infinite cancel-loop churn; gh-748 interplay documented).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/tick with a validating PR whose only run is cancelled ⇒ same tick re-dispatches and logs the zombie line; mutex not blocking other candidates during the same tick.
2. AC2: after 3 consecutive zombie cycles on one head ⇒ `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, no silent loop).
3. AC3: a live running validation still holds the mutex exactly as today (no behavior change for healthy flow).
4. AC4: live verification on the next cancelled-run occurrence in fa — recovery ≤ 1 tick, zero manual dispatches.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the liveness state machine (running/concluded/zombie/park).
- L2: replay the #1443 timeline (armed → cancelled → 2h hold) against the new rule — recovery at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next real occurrence recovers without manual action (I verify).

## Non-goals

- Parallel validations (serial mutex stays).
- Changing kicker/dispatch race guard gh-748 itself (zombie rule composes with it).

## References

- Instance: dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09 (fa PR #1443, runs 12:28 failure / 13:36 cancelled).
- Related: #806 (arming latch — same single-flight philosophy), #682/#748 (cancel-loop family).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 822
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/822
- **Title**: gh-821 [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-821` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +709
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:00:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T16:27:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #821
### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).
- `sm_github.json`: sweep rule description documents the amendment + knobs (`zombieRedispatchCap` default 3, `zombieRedispatchMinMs` default 3600000).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` — L1 liveness state machine (running / green / red / zombie-cancelled / zombie-no-run / fail-safe probes) + marker round-trip, per-head counts, cap/window knobs: 16 cases.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 8 sweep cases: AC1 #1443 replay (cancelled 2h ⇒ recovery at tick 1, arm re-acquired, zombie line logged), no-run zombie, AC2 crash-loop park (no 4th dispatch), bound hold + bound expiry, AC3 live-run no-churn, fresh-cancel race window preserved, DRY no-side-effects. Verified RED on the pre-fix engine (3 new behaviors fail at baseline `58a2dbf`), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2204 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes

- Probe-error degeneracy is deliberate: `newestDispatchedRun` fails closed (null), so a degraded read classifies `zombie-no-run` — worst case one bounded duplicate CI run (1/head/hour), never a wedge; a wrongful `running` classification would re-create the deadlock.
- The zombie branch composes with gh-748 (belt check: any run on the head active or completed within the dispatch-race grace keeps the arm) and leaves gh-755 / rerun-cancelled-checks untouched — fresh cancellations still read `running` for their first 15 minutes.
- AC4 (live fa verification on the next cancelled run) is owner-verified; expected recovery ≤ 2 ticks (~15-min visibility grace + one 10-min cadence) instead of a manual unstick.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | …

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

### Path stability
Do not rename or move root `*.json` config files — CI workflows and Jira automations reference them by path. Safe refactors: splitting prompt markdown, adding instruction files, adding `cliPrompts` composition in target repos.

### Thread 1 — `js/smAgent.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
🚨 **BLOCKING: unguarded `dispatchCiWorkflow` in the zombie re-dispatch path — a throwing dispatch aborts the entire SM tick**

The zombie re-dispatch sequence strips the arm, then calls the dispatch **outside any try/catch** (js/smAgent.js:2777):

```js
try {
    if (!DRY) {
        github_remove_label({ ... label: 'ai_validating' ... });
    }
} catch (eZun) { /* absent arm is fine */ }
dropOpenPrsCache(effectiveRepoInfo);
dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);   // ← unguarded
```

Every other localAction contains its per-ticket failures: `validate_pr` wraps the **identical** `dispatchCiWorkflow` call (js/smAgent.js:2062) in its whole-body try/catch, and `headWorkflowRunsSafe` exists specifically because `cli_execute_command` throws ("a probe error must not kill the action"). If `gh workflow run` throws here — transient gh/API failure, network hiccup, auth blip — the exception propagates out of the tickets loop and `processRule` (the `rules.forEach` at js/smAgent.js:5090 has no try/catch either), **killing the whole SM tick**: every remaining rule and every remaining PR in the window is skipped for that cadence. That is exactly the merge-window-starvation class of incident gh-821 exists to eliminate, reintroduced on the degraded-infrastructure path where throws are most likely.

It also leaves the PR half-transitioned: the arm is already stripped, the dispatch failed, the re-arm never runs, and — worst — the **marker comment is never posted**, so the crash-loop counter under-counts and the 1/head/hour bound cannot fire for that lost dispatch.

Fix (mirrors the file's own convention):

```js
try {
    dispatchCiWorkflow(ticket.branch);
} catch (eZci) {
    console.warn('  ⚠️  zombie re-dispatch failed for ' + key + ': ' + (eZci.message || eZci) +
                 ' — re-arming, retry next tick');
    try {
        if (!DRY) {
            github_add_labels({
                workspace: effectiveRepoInfo.owner, repository: effectiveRepoInfo.repo,
                number: ticket.prNumber, labels: ['ai_validating']
            });
        }
    } catch (eZre2) { /* validate-armed re-arms next tick anyway */ }
    continue;
}
```

(Restore the arm on dispatch failure so the PR keeps its serialization slot and the next tick retries as a zombie instead of re-entering the arm race through `validate-armed`.)

---

### Thread 2 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `classify()` JSDoc contradicts the deliberate fail-closed degeneracy**

The docstring says:

But the module's own header (lines 30–36) and the `classify({})` test ("a truthy probe with NO facets reads as zombie-no-run — deliberate gh-821 bias") codify the opposite for the *realistic* degraded shape: a full probe failure yields `{ active: false, newest: null }` → **`zombie-no-run` → re-dispatch**, not `'running'`. Only a *missing* probe argument (`classify(null)`) and per-facet oddities fall safe to `'running'`.

This matters beyond wording: the next maintainer reading the `classify()` contract could "fix" the discrepancy by making degraded probes read `'running'` — which the header explicitly warns would re-create the deadlock (`the alternative (treating a probe outage as live) re-creates the deadlock this module exists to break`). Please reword the last docstring paragraph to match the implemented, tested contract, e.g.:

 * Missing probe / odd per-facet shapes fail SAFE toward 'running' (arm
 * stays). A fully-failed probe (every facet at its catch default) reads
 * 'zombie-no-run' — the deliberate gh-821 bias documented in the header:
 * worst case one bounded duplicate CI run, never a wedge.
```

### Thread 3 — `js/common/validationLiveness.js`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` is a dead export**

`js/common/validationLiveness.js:46` exports `ACTIVE_RUN_STATES`, justified as "the same vocabulary hasActiveDispatchedRun / hasActiveHeadRun match in smAgent" — but nothing consumes it: `hasActiveDispatchedRun`, the `PROBE_WORKER_SOURCE` copy, and `hasActiveHeadRun` all keep their own inline `queued/in_progress/waiting/pending` lists, and no test references the constant.

# gh-821: [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)

## Description

## Goal

A validating PR whose head has no live validation run must re-dispatch within the tick instead of holding the serial `ai_validating` mutex — a cancelled/failed-concluded dispatch must never block the whole merge window.

## Subject

Tick's validating-state handling (fa `machine-sm.yml` engine + dmtools-agents arming rules). Live incident 2026-10-09 13:36–15:00Z: fa PR #1443 armed `ai_validating`; its dispatched run concluded **cancelled** (kicker/dispatch race, gh-748 guard family); the sweep kept the arm ("no concluded-and-stale validation run on the head — arm stays") while four validated PRs deferred on `🔒 mutex ai_validating held`. Merge window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>` unstick. Instance logged on #682.

## Capability surface

- Liveness probe: for each `ai_validating` PR, resolve its head's dispatch runs; states: running (in-flight), concluded-success/failure (verdict path), cancelled/stale-with-no-run (zombie).
- Zombie rule: cancelled-only or no-run ⇒ re-dispatch validation same tick (bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour; log `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`).
- Mutex fairness: the `ai_validating` mutex must be held only while a LIVE run exists; zombie ⇒ release the slot for the window (the re-dispatch re-acquires).
- Crash-loop guard: 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ park `validation_failed` + comment (avoid infinite cancel-loop churn; gh-748 interplay documented).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: sim/tick with a validating PR whose only run is cancelled ⇒ same tick re-dispatches and logs the zombie line; mutex not blocking other candidates during the same tick.
2. AC2: after 3 consecutive zombie cycles on one head ⇒ `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed, no silent loop).
3. AC3: a live running validation still holds the mutex exactly as today (no behavior change for healthy flow).
4. AC4: live verification on the next cancelled-run occurrence in fa — recovery ≤ 1 tick, zero manual dispatches.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests for the liveness state machine (running/concluded/zombie/park).
- L2: replay the #1443 timeline (armed → cancelled → 2h hold) against the new rule — recovery at tick 1.
- L3 (live): next real occurrence recovers without manual action (I verify).

## Non-goals

- Parallel validations (serial mutex stays).
- Changing kicker/dispatch race guard gh-748 itself (zombie rule composes with it).

## References

- Instance: dmtools-agents #682 comment 2026-10-09 (fa PR #1443, runs 12:28 failure / 13:36 cancelled).
- Related: #806 (arming latch — same single-flight philosophy), #682/#748 (cancel-loop family).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 822
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/822
- **Title**: gh-821 [BUG] Validating PR dead-holds the ai_validating mutex on a cancelled dispatch — merge window idle 2h (fa PR #1443)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-821` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +709
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T16:00:50Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T16:27:21Z

## PR Description

Closes #821
### Root Cause

A validating PR whose dispatched validation run concluded `cancelled` (or whose dispatch was lost) kept the `ai_validating` arm forever: `sweep_stale_validation` (`js/smAgent.js`) only sweeps arms whose run concluded a *verdict* — `CANCELLED is never a verdict` (gh-755) — so a cancelled-only / no-run head hit the `!sOld` "arm stays" branch every tick. The arm held the serial merge-window mutex with no live run behind it, and `validate-armed`'s mutex scan deferred every other approved candidate (`js/sm/sources/githubSource.js`). Live: fa PR #1443 armed 2026-10-09, run concluded cancelled 13:36Z, four validated PRs deferred, window idle ~2h until a manual `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <head>`.

### Fix

- `js/common/validationLiveness.js` (new, pure): liveness state machine over the dispatched-run probe — `running` (in-flight, or concluded inside the 15-min check-visibility grace, so the gh-748 race window and the rerun-cancelled-checks remedy keep the first minutes), `green`/`red` (existing verdict paths, untouched), `zombie-cancelled` / `zombie-no-run`.
- `sweep_stale_validation` zombie branch: same-tick re-dispatch — release the `ai_validating` slot, dispatch CI on the dead head, re-acquire the arm (the mutex is held only while a LIVE run exists; serial mutex intact, no parallel validations), logging `🔄 re-dispatching zombie validation for pr-N`. Bounded: 1 auto re-dispatch per head per hour via marker-comment bookkeeping (same carrier as the red-head markers); 3 zombie re-dispatches in a row on the same head ⇒ unarm + `validation_failed` park + explanatory comment (fail-closed; a new head SHA restarts validation via the #633/gh-750 reset probes). A live run keeps the arm exactly as today (AC3 — healthy flow unchanged).
- `sm_github.json`: sweep rule description documents the amendment + knobs (`zombieRedispatchCap` default 3, `zombieRedispatchMinMs` default 3600000).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_validationLiveness.js` — L1 liveness state machine (running / green / red / zombie-cancelled / zombie-no-run / fail-safe probes) + marker round-trip, per-head counts, cap/window knobs: 16 cases.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 8 sweep cases: AC1 #1443 replay (cancelled 2h ⇒ recovery at tick 1, arm re-acquired, zombie line logged), no-run zombie, AC2 crash-loop park (no 4th dispatch), bound hold + bound expiry, AC3 live-run no-churn, fresh-cancel race window preserved, DRY no-side-effects. Verified RED on the pre-fix engine (3 new behaviors fail at baseline `58a2dbf`), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2204 passed, 0 failed.

### Notes

- Probe-error degeneracy is deliberate: `newestDispatchedRun` fails closed (null), so a degraded read classifies `zombie-no-run` — worst case one bounded duplicate CI run (1/head/hour), never a wedge; a wrongful `running` classification would re-create the deadlock.
- The zombie branch composes with gh-748 (belt check: any run on the head active or completed within the dispatch-race grace keeps the arm) and leaves gh-755 / rerun-cancelled-checks untouched — fresh cancellations still read `running` for their first 15 minutes.
- AC4 (live fa verification on the next cancelled run) is owner-verified; expected recovery ≤ 2 ticks (~15-min visibility grace + one 10-min cadence) instead of a manual unstick.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | …
